messages:
Maya: FYI I opened PR #4821 to update stellaris7b model card with new limits (max_tokens 8192 -> 12288) and fresh bench numbers. Need a quick review on the sample prompts and SDK snippets.
Sam: Link? I can take a look this afternoon.
Maya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4821 — includes a new p50/p95/p99 latency table plus a short note on warm vs cold start behavior.
Elaine: Quick skim: bench numbers look reasonable but the embeddings throughput row reads 4k qps for 8k seq which seems off (looks like an old shard config slipped in).
Maya: Good catch — that was from the legacy shard setup. I re-ran the harness with bench-tag 'stellaris-v2' and updated the table. Bench output excerpt below:
```
# bench summary (stellaris-v2)
p50: 18ms
p95: 120ms
p99: 320ms
throughput: 720 tokens/s per GPU
```
Sam: Can you paste the SDK snippet you want in the card? I want to confirm we use SDK v3 idioms (async + streaming example).
Maya: Current draft was still SDK v2, I rewrote the simple sync example to python v3 but we should show async streaming too. Current sync snippet in PR: 
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
client.generate(model='stellaris7b', prompt='hello world', max_tokens=256)
```
Maya: I'll add an async streaming variant and a TypeScript example as well.
Tim: Also add a compatibility note: 4-bit quantized variants are only supported on Dedicated and Private deployments — CPU fallback/edge runtimes are not supported for quantized stellaris7b. Make the deprecation/compatibility language explicit.
Nina: Also the bench artifact links in the draft are 404. Correct link is https://bench.redwood/reports/stellaris-v2 — please update.
docs-bot: CI lint failed: markdown anchor 'limits' not found, suggested 'capacity-limits' anchor.
Maya: I'll push the anchor fix and the updated links in a follow-up commit.
Sam: Ping me when done, I'll review the SDK snippets (TS + async) and the migration note for stellaris6b -> stellaris7b.
Elaine: Also suggest adding a short prompt-set example that demonstrates long-context behavior and token-trimming strategy for users migrating from smaller models. A one-paragraph migration guide would help.
Maya: Added a migration blurb and a prompt truncation snippet in the PR; also added a simple long-context example set under docs/examples/stellaris/long_context.md. PTAL @Sam @Elaine
Sam: Reviewing now. If the async stream shows the right partial-chunk API it should be good.
Elaine: LGTM for the migration blurb. One nit: reword the 'throughput' row to make it explicit that numbers are tokens/sec/GPU with batching=auto.
Maya: Fixed wording and updated the bench table caption. Also added a changelog entry in docs/CHANGELOG.md describing the limits bump and compatibility note.
Tim: +1. Once CI is green we can merge. :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks all — will merge after pipeline passes.
